title: Remove Outermost Parentheses
description:
A valid parentheses string `s` is *primitive* if it is non-empty and cannot be split into two non-empty valid parentheses strings `A + B`.

Given a valid parentheses string `s`, consider its primitive decomposition `s = P_1 + P_2 + ... + P_k`, where each `P_i` is a primitive valid parentheses string. Return `s` after removing the outermost `'('` and `')'` of every primitive string in its primitive decomposition.
constraints: s is a valid parentheses string.
hints: Track the current open-parenthesis depth as you scan s from left to right.
Include '(' only when depth > 0 before incrementing, and include ')' only when depth > 0 after decrementing.

examples.explanation: Primitive decomposition is "(()())" + "(())"; removing outer parentheses gives "()()" + "()" = "()()()".
Primitive decomposition is "()" + "()"; stripping outer parentheses leaves "".
